label: Long-sequence (L=9) delimiter step, plus late copy steps reading 2/o/u/p
explanation: Only active after the original phase (never at t < L) and almost only for long sequences: L=9 holds 91% of activation mass, L=8 holds 9%, and L<=7 essentially none. The main mode is the <DEL> step of L=9 sequences, which holds about 61% of mass and every top activation. It fires on only about 40% of those delimiters, and which ones depends on content: firing is more likely when the next output orig(1) is m/x/h/i/d/o, but no simple rule separates them. The weaker second mode is late copy steps (recall_idx 6-8, rate rising toward the last output) whose input token is 2, o, u or p; 2 and o dominate. It never fires during original-token input. It is rare at early copy steps and on short sequences. Predicate dev F1 0.51, mass recall 0.82; precision stays limited by the content-dependent delimiter firing.
